title: Edge Mesh: A New Paradigm to Enable Distributed Intelligence in Internet of Things
research_problem: IoT architectures send data to centralised clouds and leave low-level edge devices out of decision-making.
approach: Edge Mesh, a paradigm that distributes decision-making tasks across a mesh network of edge devices and routers, with a proposed software framework.
key_contribution: Defines the Edge Mesh paradigm and its benefits (distributed processing, low latency, fault tolerance, scalability, privacy) along with its research challenges.
edge_relevance: IoT and Edge/Fog Computing (Computer Networks and Communications)

title: EdgeShard: Efficient LLM Inference via Collaborative Edge Computing
research_problem: LLMs deployed in the cloud incur latency, bandwidth cost and privacy concerns, yet single edge devices cannot host them, and compression costs accuracy.
approach: EdgeShard partitions an LLM into shards across collaborating edge devices and cloud servers, jointly choosing devices and partitions with a dynamic-programming algorithm.
key_contribution: The first collaborative-edge LLM inference approach, optimising latency and throughput without accuracy loss.
edge_relevance: Blockchain Technology Applications and Security (Information Systems)

title: A Learning-Based Incentive Mechanism for Federated Learning
research_problem: Federated learning needs edge nodes to contribute training, but existing incentive mechanisms fail because contributions are hard to evaluate and information is not shared.
approach: A deep-reinforcement-learning incentive mechanism that learns the parameter server's pricing strategy and the edge nodes' training strategies.
key_contribution: A learning-based incentive mechanism for federated learning, evaluated in numerical experiments.

title: Wireless Powered Mobile Edge Computing Networks: A Survey
research_problem: Wireless-powered mobile edge computing must jointly design offloading and resource allocation under time-varying channels, coupled battery levels and half-duplex devices.
approach: Survey of the WPMEC system model, key issues and techniques, and offloading and resource-allocation solutions.
key_contribution: A structured review of wireless-powered MEC with open research challenges.
edge_relevance: IoT and Edge/Fog Computing (Computer Networks and Communications)

title: Markov Approximation for Combinatorial Network Optimization
research_problem: Many network design problems are combinatorial and hard to solve with distributed algorithms.
approach: Markov approximation: approximating the optimum with a log-sum-exp function whose solution is the stationary distribution of time-reversible Markov chains that can be run distributedly.
key_contribution: A general framework for designing distributed algorithms with provable performance, illustrated through three network applications.
edge_relevance: Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (Computer Networks and Communications)

title: Unsupervised Learning for Solving AC Optimal Power Flows: Design, Analysis, and Experiment
research_problem: Supervised learning for AC optimal power flow needs costly labelled solutions and suffers when multiple load-solution mappings exist.
approach: DeepOPF-NGT, an unsupervised approach with a purpose-designed loss, Kron reduction and an adaptive learning rate that balances gradient contributions.
key_contribution: Optimality, feasibility and speed comparable to supervised methods without ground-truth solutions, shown on 39- to 1,354-bus systems.
edge_relevance: Energy Load and Power Forecasting (Electrical and Electronic Engineering)

title: Task Co-Offloading for D2D-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing in Industrial Internet of Things
research_problem: Industrial IoT tasks can be offloaded to MEC servers or nearby devices, but mobility, selfish devices and incomplete information make co-offloading hard.
approach: A co-offloading framework that accounts for migration cost and offloading willingness, with a learning-based algorithm for choosing edge nodes.
key_contribution: Lower system cost (task delay plus migration cost) without needing complete offloading information, verified in simulation.
edge_relevance: IoT and Edge/Fog Computing (Computer Networks and Communications)

title: Enabling Cost-Effective, SLO-Aware Machine Learning Inference Serving on Public Cloud
research_problem: ML inference serving on public clouds must meet response-time SLOs for dynamic workloads while keeping cost low.
approach: MArk combines dynamic batching on GPUs, predictive autoscaling, and serverless instances to absorb unpredictable load spikes.
key_contribution: An SLO-aware, cost-effective inference serving system that reduces serving cost compared with AWS SageMaker.
edge_relevance: Cloud Computing and Resource Management (Information Systems)

title: DL2: A Deep Learning-Driven Scheduler for Deep Learning Clusters
venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
research_problem: Cluster schedulers for deep-learning jobs are either unaware of ML workload characteristics or rely on framework-specific heuristics.
approach: DL2, which warms up a neural-network scheduler with supervised learning on job traces, then fine-tunes it with online reinforcement learning to resize job resources dynamically.
key_contribution: Average job completion time 44.1% better than DRF and 17.5% better than the Optimus heuristic scheduler, implemented on Kubernetes with MXNet.
edge_relevance: Cloud Computing and Resource Management (Information Systems)

title: Task Placement and Resource Allocation for Edge Machine Learning: A GNN-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Paradigm
venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
research_problem: Edge-cloud schedulers allocate fixed requested resources to ML tasks and underuse scarce edge resources.
approach: TapFinger, a distributed scheduler that co-optimises task placement and fine-grained multi-resource allocation using multi-agent reinforcement learning with a heterogeneous graph attention network.
key_contribution: Up to 54.9% lower average ML-task completion time and better resource efficiency than state-of-the-art schedulers.
edge_relevance: IoT and Edge/Fog Computing (Computer Networks and Communications)

title: vPipe: A Virtualized Acceleration System for Achieving Efficient and Scalable Pipeline Parallel DNN Training
venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
research_problem: Pipeline-parallel DNN training systems use fixed layer partitioning and memory management, causing out-of-memory errors and GPU under-utilisation.
approach: vPipe provides dynamic layer partitioning and memory management through an online planning algorithm and live layer migration across the pipeline.
key_contribution: Training throughput 61.4% to 463.4% higher than PipeDream and GPipe.
edge_relevance: Advanced Neural Network Applications (Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)

title: AoI-Aware User Service Satisfaction Enhancement in Digital Twin-Empowered Edge Computing
research_problem: Object mobility and dynamic query arrivals make it hard to keep digital-twin data fresh (measured by Age of Information) in mobile edge computing.
approach: An AoI-based user satisfaction metric, with static and dynamic digital-twin placement problems solved by an ILP and performance-guaranteed algorithms.
key_contribution: Digital-twin placement algorithms for MEC that improve user service satisfaction.
edge_relevance: Age of Information Optimization (Computer Networks and Communications)

title: Resource-Efficient Collaborative Edge Transformer Inference With Hybrid Model Parallelism
research_problem: Transformer inference on a single edge device is limited by compute and memory, while cloud offloading raises network-load and privacy concerns.
approach: Galaxy+ uses hybrid model parallelism across trusted nearby edge devices, heterogeneity- and memory-aware planning, tile-based overlap of communication and computation, and fault-tolerant rescheduling.
key_contribution: A collaborative edge system for resource-efficient Transformer inference across heterogeneous devices.
edge_relevance: Advanced Data Compression Techniques (Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)

title: Matrix-Based Evolutionary Computation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence
research_problem: Evolutionary computation algorithms become slow and computationally heavy on large-scale optimisation problems.
approach: Matrix-based evolutionary computation, which represents the whole population as a matrix so that evolutionary operators run as parallel matrix operations.
key_contribution: A framework for scaling evolutionary algorithms to very large problems, with two example MEC algorithms.

title: Exploring the application of ChatGPT in ESL/EFL education and related research issues: a systematic review of empirical studies
research_problem: ChatGPT is widely used in ESL/EFL education, but no systematic review had summarised the evidence and the gaps.
approach: Systematic review of 70 empirical studies from the 18 months after ChatGPT's release, using the Technology-based Learning Model.
key_contribution: Maps where ChatGPT has been applied in language education and its benefits and drawbacks, and finds most studies focus on writing with little quantitative evidence.
edge_relevance: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education (Health Informatics)
